label: Moving house

what_happens.title: What happens when we move
goals: The steps: pack boxes, say goodbye to the old home, the truck, the new home, unpack, first night
All our things come with us in boxes
what_happens.parentSkill: Name the moving steps in order and mark moving day on a calendar together.

who_is_there.title: Who helps us move
goals: Movers carry heavy boxes and furniture onto a truck
The family stays together, and a grown-up says where the child will be on moving day
New neighbours and maybe new friends live near the new home
who_is_there.parentSkill: Say who will look after your child on moving day and where they will be.

what_i_do.title: What I do when we move
goals: Pack my own special box and draw on it
Say goodbye to my old room
Choose where my toys go in the new room
what_i_do.parentSkill: Give your child one real job: packing and labelling their own special box.

if_scared.title: If moving feels hard
goals: The home looks different with boxes, and new rooms smell and sound new
Missing the old home is okay, and happy and sad can come together
Calm tools: the special box, a goodbye walk, a photo of the old room, slow breaths
if_scared.parentSkill: Let your child miss the old home out loud: 'You'll miss your room. I will too.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise moving day
goals: Pack a toy box like a mover, then unpack it in a new spot
Make a goodbye list and a hello list
Say the moving steps once more, ending with the first night in the new bed
rehearsal.parentSkill: Pack and unpack a toy box together, then make a goodbye list and a hello list.

steps: Pack my own special box and draw on it
Say goodbye to each room of the old home
Movers carry the boxes onto a big truck
Open my special box first and set up my room
Sleep the first night in my bed in the new home
sensory: the sound of packing tape going zzzip
a big truck with a loud ramp
new smells and new sounds at night
my own blanket and pillow in a new room
honestyNotes: Moving is a big change, and feelings can be mixed for weeks. Do not promise that the child will love the new home or make friends right away. Say what stays the same: the family, the toys, the bed and the bedtime routine.

fallbackAnswer: Yes. All your toys come in boxes on the truck.
Your special box rides with us, so you can open it first.

questionButtons.text: Can we visit the old home?
fallbackAnswer: Someone new will live there, so we might not go inside again.
We can take photos and say goodbye to each room before we go.
Making new friends can take a little time.
We can say hello to neighbours and keep in touch with old friends too.

questionButtons.text: Will I have my own bed?
fallbackAnswer: Yes. Your bed comes with us, and your blanket and pillow too.
We will set it up on the first day.
Movers are strong helpers whose job is to carry boxes and furniture.
They are careful with our things.
Moving can feel happy and sad at the same time.
It is okay to miss the old home, and I miss it too sometimes.

questionButtons.text: Where will I be on moving day?
fallbackAnswer: [[GROWNUP]] will tell you exactly where you will be and who is with you.
You will be with the family again in the new home by bedtime.
Every home has its own sounds, like pipes, cars or wind.
After a few nights, the new sounds start to feel normal.

techniques.label: Packing a special box
techniques.how: Let your child pack and decorate one box with favourite things; carry it in the car and open it first.

techniques.label: A goodbye walk
techniques.how: Walk through each room of the old home and say goodbye out loud; take a photo of each.

techniques.label: Keeping bedtime the same
techniques.how: Keep the same bedtime story, song and order on the first nights in the new home.

techniques.label: Choosing where things go
techniques.how: Let your child decide where the bed, toys or pictures go in the new room.

techniques.label: A hello walk
techniques.how: Walk around the new street, find a park or a shop, and say hello to a neighbour.

techniques.label: A photo book of old and new
techniques.how: Make a small photo book: the old home, the new home and the people in both.

techniques.label: A night light
techniques.how: Use a night light and the familiar blanket for the first nights to soften new sounds and shadows.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Calling an old friend
techniques.how: Plan a video call or a letter to an old friend in the first week.

ritual: Put my blanket on my bed
Say goodnight to my new room

pain: Moving can make your heart feel sore. That makes sense.
Let's have a big hug and take a slow breath.
separation: We all move together. The family stays the same.
Here is where you will be on moving day and who is with you.
unknown: First boxes, then the truck, then the new home, then your bed.
Your special box comes in the car with us.
strangers: The movers' job is to carry heavy things carefully.
Let's say hello to a new neighbour.
sensory: New homes have new sounds. They feel normal after a few nights.
safety: Your bed comes with us, and we will set it up on the first day.
Bedtime stays the same in the new home.
social: New friends take time. We can keep old friends too.
Let's find the park near the new home.
body: You can choose where your toys go.
Show me where you want your bed.
love: It's okay to miss the old home. I love you here and there.
Wherever we live, we are a family.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]]'s family will move to a new home.
Moving means taking all our things to live in a different place.
First, everything gets packed into brown boxes.
Zzzip goes the tape.
Toys, books, plates and pillows all go in.
Then the boxes wait in a big tower.
On moving day, a big truck comes.
The boxes and the beds ride in the truck.
Then the whole family drives to the new home together.
After that, the boxes come inside, and the family unpacks.
Last of all, [[CHILD]] sleeps in the same bed, in a new room.
On moving day there are movers.
Movers are strong helpers.
Their job is to carry heavy boxes and furniture onto the truck.
They are careful with every box, even the special one.
[[CHILD]] can say hello and watch them go up the ramp.
[[GROWNUP]] tells [[CHILD]] where [[CHILD]] will be on moving day, and who is with [[CHILD]].
The family stays together, and by bedtime everyone is in the new home.
Near the new home there are neighbours, and maybe a park with other kids.
[[CHILD]] can wave hello to someone new.
[[CHILD]] has a very important moving job.
[[CHILD]] gets one special box.
[[CHILD]] chooses what goes inside: a favourite toy, a book, a night light.
Then [[CHILD]] draws on the box so everyone knows it is special.
The special box rides in the car with the family, and it opens first.
Before moving day, [[CHILD]] says goodbye to the old room.
Goodbye, window. Goodbye, door.
[[CHILD]] can take a photo to remember.
In the new home, [[CHILD]] decides where the toys go and where the pictures hang.
Choosing makes the new room feel like [[CHILD]]'s own.
When things are packed, the old home can look strange.
Empty rooms make echoes.
The new home has new smells and new sounds at night, like pipes or cars.
It can feel strange at first, and that is okay.
After a few nights, the new sounds start to feel normal.
Sometimes [[CHILD]] might miss the old home.
Happy and sad can come at the same time.
It is okay to miss things, and [[GROWNUP]] misses them too.
[[CHILD]]'s bed, blanket and bedtime story come along.
[[CHILD]] can hug the blanket and take slow breaths.
Tonight [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] play movers.
First, they pack a toy box and tape it shut, zzzip.
Then [[CHILD]] carries it like a strong mover to a new spot.
Next, they open it and find a new place for each toy.
Where should the bear live now?
Let's say the moving steps once more.
First, pack the boxes and the special box.
Then, goodbye to the old rooms.
Next, the truck and the drive.
Last, the special box opens, and the first night in the new home.
[[GROWNUP]] is proud of [[CHILD]] and gives a big hug.
